description: A WireGuard interface of the router, named as the document: its UDP port, its addresses, its VRF and the Secret key that holds its private key. Its peers are WireGuardPeer documents.

addresses.description: Addresses of the interface with their prefix lengths, as `Address=` of a `Network` gives them; the router routes each prefix to the interface. The peers' `allowedIPs` add routes of their own.

listenPort.description: UDP port the interface receives its peers' packets on, which the firewall opens in the default VRF. Two WireGuards take different ports.

x-chalkos-unique.hint: give each WireGuard a port of its own

mtu.description: MTU of the interface in bytes, from 1280 to 9000; null takes WireGuard's 1420.

privateKey.description: Key of a Secret that holds the interface's private key, as `wg genkey` prints it. systemd-networkd reads it from its credentials; no rendered file holds it. The Secret's name and key hold letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-` alone.

x-chalkos-rules.description: A WireGuard key names its Secret and key as credentials' names.
x-chalkos-rules.message: the Secret's name and key of privateKey hold letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-' alone, as the names of systemd-networkd's credentials do

vrf.description: VRF document that holds the interface; `default` for the default VRF. The routes of the peers' `allowedIPs` go into the VRF's table; the tunnel's own UDP packets travel in the default VRF whatever this says.

title: WireGuard

rules.description: A WireGuard is named as its interface, in 15 characters at most.
rules.messageExpression: documents.filter(n, size(n) > 15).map(n, "WireGuard " + n).join(", ") + " has a name of more than 15 characters, which is no interface's name; give it a shorter one"

rules.description: A WireGuard's name does not start with n64-, which starts the names of the NAT64s' links.
rules.messageExpression: documents.filter(n, n.startsWith("n64-")).map(n, "WireGuard " + n).join(", ") + ": n64- starts the names of the NAT64s' links; give the WireGuard another name"

rules.description: A WireGuard does not take the name of a VRF, whose device has it.
rules.messageExpression: cel.bind(vrfs, (("router.chalkos.dev/v1alpha1" in config && "VRF" in config["router.chalkos.dev/v1alpha1"]) ? config["router.chalkos.dev/v1alpha1"].VRF : {}), documents.filter(n, n in vrfs).map(n, "WireGuard " + n).join(", ") + " takes the name of a VRF, whose device has it; give the WireGuard another name")
rules.rule: cel.bind(vrfs, (("router.chalkos.dev/v1alpha1" in config && "VRF" in config["router.chalkos.dev/v1alpha1"]) ? config["router.chalkos.dev/v1alpha1"].VRF : {}), documents.all(n, !(n in vrfs)))
